Current assessment — 2026-10-05

Reviewed against local main 7057a8d5a2d898c1bfb528a28f3f635dda639b8b, origin/main 568ce108 (local main clean, 112 ahead/0 behind at audit; no push).

Where we are: The amended v0b type-B normalization/parity gate is recovered on main. Consolidation recreated an isolated hash-locked GLMsingle environment at pinned upstream 1ab54a65 and passed all required real bridge checks. This does not supply type-D scientific equivalence or Linux custody admission.

Fresh context: Yes: delivered gate / runtime reconciliation.

Next action: Reconcile exact upstream/runtime/units and owner-amended bound with the delivered gate record; preserve the original literal-bound failure and unseen-design evidence. Recreate runtime from locks when resuming rather than using incomplete old .venv links.

Evidence: v0b gate note; docs/verification/phrf-pilot-integration-20261004.md; docs/verification/consolidation-20261005.md.

This is a tracker/source/retained-evidence assessment, not a new experiment or test run. Existing acceptance criteria and owner decisions remain binding; dated source-state statements below are superseded where this assessment explicitly corrects them. Status, priority, assignee, claims and dependency edges are unchanged.

---

Previous scope and history (acceptance retained)

Pilot-scoped harness slice (owner D1). Per protocol v3.1 §4 F10 and v0. Pin the official GLMsingle (Prince et al. 2022) at an exact commit and install it in an isolated venv (no global installs). Verify from its source and with a numeric check: beta units (percent signal change or not), the HRF library normalization, the type B/C/D outputs, and a low-noise (SNR 100) parity check for types C/D. If the gate fails, D5 becomes 'not run' before the pilot. Record the provenance and licence.
